tool.name: RadiatingLines

summary.para: Generates evenly spaced lines radiating outward from every input point, and/or a point feature class of the origins and line endpoints -- regularly spaced sampling locations around points of interest. Give the number of lines or the bearing interval, and a line length in real units; the first bearing points north or is randomized (seed-reproducible), the rest follow clockwise. New in this version: lines can be blocked by any number of barrier polyline and polygon feature classes -- a line stops at its first crossing of a barrier line or polygon boundary (an origin inside a barrier polygon still radiates), with a Blocked flag. A modernized port of Jeff Jenness's classic ArcView Radiating Lines and Points extension, originally written for the study published as Ekebom et al. (2003). Works at every license level.

tool.usage:
Casts a fan of evenly spaced lines outward from every input point -- the classic way to lay out regularly spaced sampling locations around points of interest, transect starts around stations, or exposure rays around sites. The outputs are the lines themselves and/or a point feature class holding each origin and every line endpoint.
The classic design, kept intact. Give either the number of lines or the bearing interval -- they are two views of one choice, and typing either fills in the other (13 lines means one every 27.6923 degrees). The first line points due north unless Randomize the first bearing spins the whole fan by a random fraction of the interval (reproducible with the seed); the remaining lines follow clockwise at the regular interval. Layer selections on the input points are honored.
Modernized distances. The original worked in raw map units and advised projecting first; here the line length is in real units (meters, kilometers, feet or miles), and geographic (latitude/longitude) points each get their own azimuthal-equidistant projection -- so every radial distance is a true geodesic and every bearing a true azimuth, at any latitude.
Barriers (new). Any number of barrier polyline and polygon feature classes stop the lines: a radiating line ends at its first crossing of a barrier line or polygon boundary, its Length_m records the truncated distance, and Blocked = 1 marks it. It is the polygon boundary that blocks, not the polygon's interior -- so an origin point sitting inside a barrier polygon still gets its full fan of lines, each one stopping where it reaches the boundary from the inside. Selections on the barrier layers are honored, the barriers may be in any mix of coordinate systems, and true-curve barriers are densified automatically. Use shorelines, roads, fences or habitat edges as barriers to turn a plain fan into a line-of-open-passage analysis -- the same ray casting that powers the Longest Line in Polygon (Fetch) tool's directional mode.
Outputs. The lines feature class carries Src_FID (the origin point's Object ID), Origin_N (the line's number around its origin, 1..k clockwise), Bearing, Length_m, Blocked, and both ends' coordinates (Org_X/Org_Y/End_X/End_Y), plus any transferred attribute fields. The points feature class holds every origin (Location = "Origin", null distance and bearing -- written as -999 in shapefiles, the classic convention) and every endpoint (Location = "End Point", with its distance and bearing), plus the same transferred fields.
Provenance. A modernized port of the ArcView 3.x "Radiating Lines and Points" extension (rad_lines.avx), which Jeff Jenness originally developed for Jan Ekebom, Pasi Laihonen and Tapio Suominen (University of Turku) for their study of Finnish coastal biodiversity, published as Ekebom, Laihonen and Suominen (2003), A GIS-based step-wise procedure for assessing physical exposure in fragmented archipelagos, Estuarine, Coastal and Shelf Science 57:887-898.

dialogReference.para: The origin points the lines radiate from. A layer selection is honored.

param.name: transfer_fields
param.displayname: Attribute fields to transfer to every output

dialogReference.para: Fields whose values ride along onto every line and point, next to the automatic Src_FID. Reserved or conflicting names arrive under a Src_ prefix with the source values intact.

param.name: n_lines
param.displayname: Number of radiating lines (or give the bearing interval below)

dialogReference.para: How many lines radiate from each point, evenly spaced around the compass. Typing a count fills in the bearing interval below, and vice versa -- give either.
The angle between successive lines. Typing an interval fills in the line count above, and vice versa -- give either. The interval is snapped so the lines divide the circle evenly.
Every line's length, in the units below -- true geodesic distances even for latitude/longitude points. Barrier crossings can shorten individual lines.
Meters, Kilometers, Feet or Miles. Output length fields are always in meters.

param.name: randomize_first
param.displayname: Randomize the first bearing (otherwise the first line points north)

dialogReference.para: Spin each point's whole fan by a random fraction of the interval, so the first line falls anywhere within the first step instead of due north. The seed makes the spin reproducible.

param.name: random_seed
param.displayname: Random seed (optional -- same seed, same bearings)

dialogReference.para: Optional: the same seed with the same inputs reproduces the same randomized bearings exactly.

param.name: block_lines
param.displayname: Barrier polylines (optional -- lines stop at the first crossing; selections honored)

dialogReference.para: One or more polyline feature classes that stop the radiating lines -- shorelines, roads, fences. A line ends at its first crossing, with Blocked = 1 and its Length_m truncated. Selections on these layers are honored.

param.name: block_polygons
param.displayname: Barrier polygons (optional -- lines stop at the polygon boundaries; selections honored)

dialogReference.para: One or more polygon feature classes whose boundaries stop the radiating lines -- habitat blocks, land masses, exclusion zones. A line ends where it first meets a polygon boundary; it is the boundary that blocks, not the interior, so an origin inside a barrier polygon still gets its full fan, each line stopping at the boundary from the inside. Selections on these layers are honored.

param.name: out_lines
param.displayname: Output radiating lines (optional -- give this, the points, or both)

dialogReference.para: The radiating lines: Src_FID, Origin_N (1..k clockwise), Bearing, Length_m, Blocked, and both ends' coordinates, plus transferred fields.

Every origin (Location = "Origin"; distance and bearing null, or -999 in shapefiles per the classic convention) and every line endpoint (Location = "End Point", with its distance and bearing), plus transferred fields.

scriptExample.title: Radiating Lines and Points example (stand-alone script)
scriptExample.para: Sixteen 500 m sampling rays around each station, blocked at the shoreline, with both outputs.
scriptExample.code: import arcpy arcpy.ImportToolbox(r"C:\path\to\JennessEnterprisesTools.pyt") # your install path # linear_units: "Meters" / "Kilometers" / "Feet" / "Miles" arcpy.jenness.RadiatingLines( points=r"D:\data\survey.gdb\stations", transfer_fields="Station_Name", n_lines=16, line_length=500.0, linear_units="Meters", randomize_first=True, random_seed=42, block_lines=r"D:\data\survey.gdb\shoreline", out_lines=r"D:\data\survey.gdb\station_rays", out_points=r"D:\data\survey.gdb\station_ray_points")
